lines.prompt: Perform depth optimization on the combinational logic while ensuring the cone of n11[0] continues to use only NAND and NOT gates. Ensure functional equivalence is preserved. The cost function is the maximum logic depth of the final design; smaller is better.

golden.reference: Depth optimization succeeded: max logic depth reduced from 49 to 10 (best observed, Team7), equivalence preserved and n11[0] cone kept in NAND/NOT basis.
golden.notes: Relative QoR line - the only fractional line for the reliable teams. Initial max depth is objectively 49 (Team3/Team4/Team7 all report it). Claimed final depths: Team7=10 (best; full case score 7/7), Team4=17, Team3=18. Score arithmetic (Team3/Team4/Team7 only): Team4's 6.59 = 6 + 10/17 matches best/achieved scaling with full credit elsewhere; Team3's 6.34 implies line credit ~0.34, which does NOT match its claimed 10/18=0.56 - consistent with the grader measuring the actual output netlist (Team3's real depth likely worse than claimed, ~29). So depth is verified on the output file, not the response text. Team2's log here shows a planner error, but that log is a different run than Team2's graded one, so no score inference from Team2 is valid. Checker: response must claim success + equivalence + NAND/NOT basis on the n11[0] cone; achieved depth is measured on the team's output netlist; score scales relative to best (10).
